selected_primary_idea.title: DNA Storage Serviceability Envelope (DSE)
selected_primary_idea.summary: A portable archive packet and multidimensional acceptance contract that evaluates DNA storage by exact, selective, condition-aware payload recovery rather than raw molecular density alone.
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: payload x coding scheme x molecular channel x storage condition x access pattern x read budget x acceptance rule
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: Joint allocation of redundancy and retrieval budgets under a portable DSE contract produces a more interpretable and transferable accepted-recovery profile than density-only evaluation.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: The archive packet makes coding, sequence constraints, indexing, storage condition, retrieval budget, decoder version, and integrity threshold explicit and testable.
falsifiers: DSE has no predictive or decision value beyond raw density
condition-aware allocation fails to match a density-only baseline under declared channels
selective recovery cannot be distinguished from whole-pool recovery
portable metadata cannot reproduce decoding in an independent software environment

competitive_ideas.title: Ultra-dense constrained code
competitive_ideas.reason: A necessary benchmark but not a complete archive-service design.

competitive_ideas.title: Compartmentalized random-access layer
competitive_ideas.reason: Potentially improves repeated access but does not make recovery portable by itself.

high_risk_ideas.title: Universal DNA storage score
high_risk_ideas.reason: Can aid comparison but may conceal noncommensurate assumptions.

rejected_ideas.reason: Archive latency and economics do not support interactive-storage replacement.

mcts_evolution.defect: raw density conflated with useful archival capacity
physical condition excluded from code choice
whole-pool decoding conflated with selective access

mcts_evolution.change: retain DSE profile and conditional decisions
